harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Provisioned an encrypted (LUKS2) volume on node1, backed by a loopback file, mounted at /srv/secure via ext4, and configured an OpenRC service (secure-volume) enabled in the default runlevel so it auto-unlocks (via a root-only keyfile) and mounts on every boot. Verified via a real node restart: boot_id changed (0f0b1874... -> 3db78b50...), the service auto-started, the LUKS2 mapping came up active, and pre-existing data on /srv/secure survived plus a post-reboot write succeeded.
actions_performed: Installed cryptsetup on node1 (Alpine 3.23, OpenRC init)
Created a 512M loopback-backed file at /var/lib/secure-volume/secure.img and a root-only keyfile at /etc/luks-keys/secure.key
luksFormat'd the loop device as LUKS2, opened it as /dev/mapper/secure_vol, formatted ext4, mounted at /srv/secure

Wrote /etc/init.d/secure-volume OpenRC script that attaches the loop device, luksOpens with the keyfile, and mounts /srv/secure on start (reverses on stop); enabled via rc-update add secure-volume default

Validated the service logic end-to-end by manually tearing down (umount/luksClose/losetup -d) and re-running rc-service secure-volume start to confirm clean-state auto-recovery before touching the real boot path
Captured pre-restart baseline (boot_id, mount, cryptsetup status, marker file, runlevel entry)
Issued sudo -n reboot on node1; acknowledgement returned before disconnect, then polled until exec access returned
Confirmed changed boot_id post-restart and verified the volume auto-unlocked/mounted, marker file intact, and a new write succeeded

evidence.requirement: Encrypted volume created and mounted at /srv/secure (initial provisioning)
evidence.summary: LUKS2 luksFormat/luksOpen on loop device, ext4 mkfs, mount at /srv/secure with marker file written; verification output shows active LUKS2 mapping and mount, plus OpenRC service installed and added to default runlevel.

Manually tore down the volume (umount, luksClose, losetup -d) and ran rc-service secure-volume start from a clean state, proving the boot-time unlock/mount logic works and data survives, before relying on an actual reboot.
Captured boot_id 0f0b1874-9005-4066-867a-2883386e7f35, active LUKS2 status, mount, marker file presence, and runlevel enablement prior to reboot.
sudo -n reboot issued in background with ack captured (REBOOT_ACK_SENT) before the exec stream closed due to the node going down.

evidence.requirement: Changed boot identity proving a real restart occurred
evidence.summary: Post-restart boot_id read as 3db78b50-5bf7-4850-b272-6fc6ae01e487, differing from the pre-restart 0f0b1874-9005-4066-867a-2883386e7f35, confirming an actual reboot (not just service restart).

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery: encrypted volume auto-unlocked/mounted and cluster/data healthy
evidence.summary: After reboot, /srv/secure is mounted from /dev/mapper/secure_vol (LUKS2, active), the secure-volume OpenRC service shows started and enabled in default runlevel, the pre-existing marker file survived, and a new write to the volume succeeded — all without manual intervention.
